homepage.kicker.message: Spring Boot multi-datasource framework · Apache-2.0 · since 2018

homepage.hero.after.message: annotation to switch datasources · local multi-DB transactions · dynamic datasource management · read-write splitting

homepage.feature.switch.desc.message: Annotate a service method with @DS("slave") to route to a database or group; SpEL keys, no-annotation approaches and the read-write splitting plugin included.

homepage.feature.pool.desc.message: First-class adapters for Druid / HikariCP / BeeCP / DBCP2 / JNDI with global and per-datasource configuration.

homepage.feature.tx.desc.message: @DSTransactional binds connections across databases under one transaction with unified commit/rollback; Seata AT/XA and Atomikos recipes included.

homepage.feature.dynamic.desc.message: Add/remove datasources at runtime, lazy startup, no-datasource startup, inventories loaded from a bootstrap DB — the foundation for multi-tenancy.

homepage.quickstart.desc.message: Add the starter, configure your databases, annotate your service methods — done.

homepage.quickstart.step1.message: 1. Configure datasources (the part before the first _ is the group name)

homepage.quickstart.more.message: Dependency coordinates (choose one per Spring Boot generation) and the full configuration reference:

homepage.skill.title.message: AI Era: put this documentation into your AI assistant

homepage.skill.desc.message: This repository ships an open-format Agent Skill. Once installed, AI coding assistants can answer questions like “why is datasource switching failing” directly in your project — installation, configuration and troubleshooting.

homepage.cta.desc.message: The most frequently reported issues (@DS not working, startup errors, no switching inside transactions) are distilled into troubleshooting checklists.

homepage.flow.title.message: How does a single request reach the right database?

homepage.flow.desc.message: Once a connection comes in, @DS resolves the target database or group, the router hands the statement to the matching datasource and returns the result the same way — none of this leaks into your business code.

homepage.flow.note.master.message: Write requests go straight to the primary

homepage.flow.scrollHint.message: ← Swipe sideways to see the full topology →
